plan.summary: Set up a professional frontend workstation: a fluent shell, Git and GitHub, a configured editor with an in-editor debugger, safe AI-assisted coding, and per-project Node.js versions.

prerequisites.bridge: Met in How to learn frontend: Git tracks changes; GitHub hosts repositories, issues and pull requests.
A process is a running program with its own input, output, environment variables and exit code.
npm installs JavaScript packages listed in package.json and runs its scripts.

outcomes: Combine shell commands with pipes, set environment variables and fix a PATH problem.
Explain Git's commit graph and choose merge or rebase for a given branch.
Find a bug-introducing commit with git bisect and recover lost work with reflog.
Open a pull request with conventional commit messages and a clean history.
Configure an editor workspace and debug JavaScript with breakpoints in the editor.
Use an AI coding agent with context, review its diff and test it before merging.
Pin a Node.js version per project and explain ESM versus CommonJS loading.

lesson_outline.title: Terminal and shell: pipes, PATH and environment
lesson_outline.visual_reason: A pipeline changes data at each stage; the learner adds and removes stages and watches the text stream change.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Build a grep | sort | uniq pipeline stage by stage and predict the output of each stage.

lesson_outline.title: Git's commit graph: branches, merge and rebase
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Merge and rebase produce different commit graphs; the learner runs each command and watches the graph change.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Run merge or rebase on the same two branches and compare the resulting graphs.

lesson_outline.title: Find and recover: bisect, reflog, stash and cherry-pick
lesson_outline.visual_reason: git bisect halves the suspect range at each step; the learner marks commits good or bad and watches the range shrink.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Mark commits good or bad and predict how many steps bisect needs.

lesson_outline.title: Pull requests, conventional commits and .gitignore
lesson_outline.visual_reason: The GitHub flow is an ordered path from branch to merged pull request; a diagram shows it.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Trace one change from a branch to a reviewed, merged pull request.

lesson_outline.title: Editor setup: workspace settings, tasks and the debugger
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Settings layers (default, user, workspace) override each other in a fixed order; a diagram shows the precedence and the debugger attach path.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Say which settings layer wins and where a breakpoint stops.

lesson_outline.title: AI-assisted development you can trust
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Safe agent use is a loop of context, tests first, generated diff, review and run; a diagram shows the gates before merge.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Sort agent outputs into merge, review further or reject.

lesson_outline.title: Node.js versions, npx and ESM versus CommonJS
lesson_outline.visual_reason: Node decides ESM or CommonJS from the file extension and the nearest package.json type field; a decision diagram shows it.
lesson_outline.interaction_goal: Predict which loader Node uses for a given file.

mini_projects.use_case: A price formatter broke somewhere in the last 30 commits; a developer scripts git bisect run with a test to find the commit that introduced the bug.
A team checks every commit message against the Conventional Commits format in a commit-msg hook and in CI, so changelogs can be generated from history.

capstone.name: devkit workstation CLI
capstone.problem: A frontend team onboards new developers often; one Node.js CLI checks the workstation (Node version against .nvmrc and engines, git identity, required tools on PATH), lints commit messages, and writes release notes from conventional commits.

goals: master frontend engineering end to end from the N1 roadmap
learn visually and by experimenting with simulations
keep improving after the roadmap ends

curriculum.scope: A frontend developer's workstation: shell fluency, Git and GitHub workflow, editor setup and debugging, responsible AI-assisted coding, and Node.js runtime and version management.

concepts.title: Finding a bad commit with git bisect
Editor setup: VS Code, JetBrains or Zed
Pinning the package manager with Corepack
Safe undo (reset, revert) and git config
Browser DevTools debugging with source maps
concepts.reason: Coverage audit round 1 (2026-11-18): no verified source in this topic covers browser DevTools or source maps; the 12-source ceiling is reached and browser debugging belongs to a later roadmap debugging/performance section.

concepts.title: Rewriting local history: amend, interactive rebase, squash
Revision selection: HEAD~n and A..B ranges
